claims.method: compares every place the release counts are published — the two homepage cards and the hero's footer line — with the data files, so no single copy can drift again. It had happened twice: the cards said 32+ and 12 before 2026-09-12, and the hero still said 32+/12 until 2026-09-15, when a rendered frame of the hero was checked by eye and the number did not match the claim.

check.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const h=fs.readFileSync('index.html','utf8');const cards=[...h.matchAll(/([0-9]+) \\u7248\\u672c<\\/span>/g)].map(m=>+m[1]);const s=fs.readFileSync('assets/hero.svg','utf8');const hero=[...s.matchAll(/OpenClaw ([0-9]+)/g)].map(m=>+m[1]).concat([...s.matchAll(/Hermes Agent ([0-9]+)/g)].map(m=>+m[1]));const r=f=>JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').match(/const [A-Z_]+ = (\\[[\\s\\S]*\\]);/)[1]).flatMap(x=>x.releases).length;const real=[r('openclaw_data.js'),r('hermes_data.js')];const all=cards.concat(hero);const ok=all.every((v,i)=>v===real[i%2]);console.log('published', all.join(','), 'vs data', real.join(','), 'match', ok);if(!ok)process.exit(1)"

claims.claim: Every page or SVG in this repository that animates also handles `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, and the artefact must stay complete when it is off.
claims.value: no animated file without a reduced-motion branch
claims.metric: files containing an animation primitive vs files containing `prefers-reduced-motion`
claims.method: the check walks every committed page and SVG and covers all four ways one can move — CSS animations/keyframes, SVG SMIL, requestAnimationFrame, and the CSS animations inside an SVG hero — requiring a `prefers-reduced-motion` reference wherever it finds one. SVG heroes are included because GitHub renders them through : scripts do not run, CSS animations do, and a hero that loops forever is exactly what a reduced-motion branch is for.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

MOVES = re.compile(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes|<animate\b|<animateTransform\b|requestAnimationFrame')
RELAX = 'prefers-reduced-motion'
pages = sorted(set(
    list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/*.svg'))
    + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('assets/readme/*.svg'))
))
pages = [p for p in pages if p.name != 'template.html']
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if MOVES.search(t):
        animated += 1
        if RELAX not in t:
            missing.append(str(p))
print('files', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert animated and not missing
PY

claims.claim: All three pages carry parseable schema.org JSON-LD, and none of them hardcodes a modified/published date — a hand-committed page with a fixed date would go stale on the next upstream release and nothing here would notice.
claims.value: 3 pages, valid JSON-LD, no hardcoded dates
claims.metric: each page's <script type=application/ld+json> block: parses, has @context/@type, has no date fields
claims.method: the check extracts the block from each of index.html, openclaw.html and hermes.html and requires it to parse as JSON with a schema.org @context and a @type, and rejects dateModified/datePublished. Dates are deliberately absent rather than checked against the data: the sync is manual, so a date would be wrong most days.

check.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const pages=['index.html','openclaw.html','hermes.html'];const bad=[];for(const p of pages){const s=fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8');const m=s.match(/<script type=\"application\/ld\+json\">\s*(\{[\s\S]*?\})\s*<\/script>/);if(!m){bad.push(p+':missing');continue;}let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[1]);}catch(e){bad.push(p+':invalid-json');continue;}if(d['@context']!=='https://schema.org')bad.push(p+':context');if(!d['@type'])bad.push(p+':type');if(/dateModified|datePublished/.test(m[1]))bad.push(p+':hardcoded-date');}console.log('pages',pages.length,'problems',JSON.stringify(bad));if(bad.length)process.exit(1)"
